paper_title: Shifting Long-Context LLMs Research from Input to Output
caption: Proportion of real-user demand: The aforementioned 2K range refers to the interval [2K, 4K), and similarly for the other ranges. Solid color fill for input demand, slash fill for output demand in the Wildchat dataset.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the proportion of real-user demand for different token length ranges, comparing input and output demands in the Wildchat dataset. The horizontal axis contains four groups of paired bars corresponding to token length ranges: 2K, 4K, 8K, and 16K, where each range represents an interval (e.g., 2K refers to [2K, 4K)). The vertical axis is labeled "Number" with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 120000, with tick marks at intervals of 20000. Each group contains two bars: one with a solid color fill representing input demand and one with a diagonal slash (hatched) fill representing output demand. For the 2K group, the solid light yellow input bar has a value of 9320 and the hatched yellow output bar has a value of 78188. For the 4K group, the solid salmon/orange input bar has a value of 3784 and the hatched orange output bar has a value of 108494, which is the tallest bar in the chart. For the 8K group, the solid light blue input bar has a value of 1401 and the hatched blue output bar has a value of 17865. For the 16K group, the solid purple input bar has a value of 832, which is the shortest bar in the chart, and the hatched purple output bar has a value of 4247. Each bar is annotated with its exact numeric value displayed above it. The bars are arranged in order from 2K to 16K from left to right, and within each group the input bar appears on the left and the output bar on the right. The legend is positioned at the bottom of the chart, showing eight entries corresponding to the four input categories (2K-Input, 4K-Input, 8K-Input, 16K-Input) and four output categories (2K-Output, 4K-Output, 8K-Output, 16K-Output).
